svg.title: Diagram of what USPS pages say about a change of address. Who and when: filed online or at a Post Office, with identity verified; a request can be submitted 90 days before the move date and up to 30 days after; the move type is Individual, Family (same last name) or Business. Online: pick a move type, verify identity with a mobile code or link and a card (an identity fee applies; the billing address must match the old or new address). At a Post Office: bring acceptable photo ID and fill in PS Form 3575; filing in person is required for a move abroad, for someone else, or if identity cannot be verified online. After filing: a letter goes to the old address and a welcome kit with a 16-digit Confirmation Code arrives about 5 business days before the start date; mail starts arriving within 7-10 business days of the start date according to the FAQ; keep the code to change or cancel. Two timing details: USPS.com says to allow at least 7-10 business days after approval for the change to go into effect, while the FAQ gives 7-10 business days after the start date for mail to arrive; and for temporary forwarding the FAQ gives a total of up to 364 days, or a first request of up to 185 days extended by up to 179 more, while USPS.com gives a range of 15 days up to 1 year.
svg.text: USPS Change of Address
What the USPS pages say
1. Who and when
Online or at a Post Office; identity must
be verified. Submit from 90 days before
the move date to 30 days after. Move
type: Individual, Family (same last
name) or Business.
2. Online
Pick a move type. Verify identity with a
mobile code or link and a card: an
identity fee applies, and the card's
billing address must match the old or
new address.
3. At a Post Office
Bring acceptable photo ID and fill in
PS Form 3575. In person is required to
move abroad, to file for someone else,
or if identity cannot be verified online.
4. After filing
A letter goes to the old address. A
welcome kit with a 16-digit Confirmation
Code arrives about 5 business days before
the start date. FAQ: mail starts arriving
within 7-10 business days of the start
date. Keep the code to change or cancel.
Two timing details
7-10 days: after approval for the change to
take effect (USPS.com); after the start date
for mail to arrive (FAQ). Temporary forwarding:
FAQ, up to 364 days in total or 185 plus up
to 179 more; USPS.com, 15 days up to 1 year.
Sources: USPS FAQ 000005313; USPS.com
Standard Forward Mail page; read Nov. 26, 2026
